problem: Instruction generators (speakers) used for data augmentation in VLN are trained with supervised losses, and generating visually grounded navigational instructions has stayed an auxiliary task rather than being optimized directly.
motivation: Better instruction generation gives better augmented data for VLN. Supervised (cross-entropy) training does not directly optimize for language quality or for how well an instruction fits its trajectory. The paper therefore uses reinforcement learning with task-relevant rewards.
key_idea: Train the instruction generator with REINFORCE, using a reward that combines BLEU, BERTScore and a VLN loss (instruction-trajectory compatibility).
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract says the approach improves the generator on the reward function itself, and it discusses reusing an existing instruction-trajectory compatibility model to train the generator.
method: REINFORCE training: the instruction generator is fine-tuned with a policy-gradient objective instead of only supervised likelihood.
Composite reward: a combination of BLEU, BERTScore and a VLN loss term.
VLN-loss reward: a navigation model's loss on the generated instruction is used as a grounding/compatibility signal.
Discussion of an instruction-trajectory compatibility model as an alternative source of reward.

setting.backbone: instruction generator (speaker) model, details not given in abstract
setting.training_data: not specified in abstract (presumably R2R instruction-trajectory pairs)

results: The abstract only says the approach improves the generation model in terms of the reward function. No numbers or baselines are given.
limitations: Improvement is reported on the reward function that was optimized, not on downstream VLN performance (per the abstract).
The compatibility-model reward is only discussed as a possibility.
